headline: Four-week volume is up 16% and easy-run cardiac drift is moving in the right direction, suggesting genuine aerobic adaptation is underway.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The most meaningful signal this week isn't the volume increase itself — it's that heart rate on comparable easy efforts has dropped noticeably since the prior block. That kind of HR shift at similar paces points to real aerobic adaptation, not just accumulated fatigue from higher load. The 20-week running streak hitting its all-time high reinforces that the consistency driving this adaptation has been sustained without interruption.

The one thing worth holding in view: strength frequency has dipped slightly relative to the prior block. Given that strength is a genuine pillar of your training — not a supplement to it — a quiet drift downward in session count is worth catching early rather than after it compounds. Nothing alarming yet, but it's the kind of thing that tends to slip further if unaddressed.
watch_items: Watch whether easy-run HR continues to decline as volume holds or builds — sustained improvement here would be a strong aerobic fitness signal.
Monitor strength session frequency over the coming fortnight; the dip is minor but worth actively countering rather than letting it drift.
After several consecutive weeks of building, pay attention to how your legs feel on back-to-back run days — cumulative fatigue can lag the acute load signal.
The lactate threshold test is recent and singular — notice whether tempo efforts feel consistent with that benchmark as more data points accumulate.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 145 km vs 125 km prior block (+16%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
